50 Ghost Ships at Rozul Reef: What China Doesn’t Want You to Notice | The presence of over 50 Chinese Maritime Militia vessels swarming Rozul Reef is not a routine patrol. It is a calculated display of dominance meant to suppress Filipino access, disrupt maritime livelihoods, and intimidate within our own waters.

Rozul Reef is 130 nautical miles from Palawan — well within the Philippines’ Exclusive Economic Zone. There is no ambiguity. Under UNCLOS, there is no legal basis for China to deploy its "ghost fleet" in these waters. No crew. No answer. No transparency. Just silent intrusion cloaked as civilian presence.

Let’s be clear:
This is not freedom of navigation.
This is illegal coercion.
This is strategic flooding of our sea lanes with militarized vessels to push the Philippines out of its rightful territory.
We will not treat these incursions as normal.
We will not be desensitized to maritime bullying disguised as routine.
And we will not let ghost ships decide the future of our living reefs, our fishers, or our sovereignty.
We stand on law.
We stand with our Coast Guard.
We stand for the West Philippine Sea.
🇵🇭 Document. Defend. Dominate the Narrative.
